mayIncludeOtherEdits.description: Something else also wrote the file while the session edited it.

changedSince.description: The file changed on the device after the session's last write.

unavailable.description: noBaseline: no copy from before the session's edits was kept.

added.description: Lines added and removed, when both sides are text.

SessionToolFrameSource.description: Where a tool frame came from (DEV-075).

SessionToolFrame.description: SessionToolFrame is a screenshot a tool call produced, which the worker keeps as a session file under the workspace's .foundry/attachments/frames (DEV-075). Events carry only this reference; the image is read on demand through the session, by those who may read the session.

callId.description: The tool call whose result carried it.

tool.description: The tool's name as the agent called it.

path.description: Absolute on the device, under the workspace's .foundry/attachments/frames.

inputId.description: The input whose turn recorded it.

AgentScheduledTask.description:
A timer/scheduled task an agent created inside its own session.
 Claude exposes session-scoped cron jobs (CronCreate/ScheduleWakeup). Claude Code fires them while its process runs and brings CronCreate jobs back when the session resumes; the device delivers a timer that comes due while no process holds the session (a ScheduleWakeup always), once, as the session's next input. Codex headless sessions have no equivalent, so timers never appear for Codex threads.

schedule.description: Raw 5-field cron expression in the wall-clock time of `timeZone`.

timeZone.description: `timeZone` is the IANA zone of the agent process that holds the timer: its cron fields are wall-clock times there, and `nextFireAt` was computed in it. It may differ from the device's own zone (a connection can set the process's TZ). Absent on timers reported before it was recorded, whose `nextFireAt` may be off by the difference.

recurring.description: false for one-shot reminders, true for recurring jobs.

prompt.description: Prompt submitted to the agent when the timer fires.

nextFireAt.description: When Claude Code fires it next (ISO 8601), its id's offset included, as of the snapshot; readers recompute it from `schedule` (in `timeZone`) as time passes. For a one-time timer with `timeZone` it is the time it fires.

createdBy.description: `createdBy` is the Claude tool that made the timer, when the device saw the call: Claude Code brings a CronCreate job back when it resumes the session, but not a ScheduleWakeup (dynamic /loop) wakeup, which the device delivers itself once it is due and no process holds it.

AgentSessionSchedule.description: AgentSessionSchedule is the timers a session's agent holds (Claude's CronCreate, ScheduleWakeup, /loop): they wake it later, so the session is not idle even when its latest input completed (Status still describes that input). Derived from the latest timer snapshot its device reported (SessionScheduleFromSnapshot).

reportedAt.description: `reportedAt` is when the device reported these timers.

AgentSessionScheduledTimer.description: AgentSessionScheduledTimer is a timer of a session's schedule, without its prompt. NextFireAt is as of ReportedAt; readers recompute it from Schedule as time passes.

timeZone.description: `timeZone` is the agent process's zone, as on AgentScheduledTask.

firstSeenAt.description: `firstSeenAt` is when a snapshot first listed the timer: a recurring one ends ClaudeRecurringTimerMaxAge later.

AgentSessionTimerFire.description: One automatic, timer-driven turn that ran without a Foundry turn open.

id.description: Scheduled task id when the firing task could be correlated.

scheduledFor.description: `scheduledFor` is when the timer was due (ISO 8601), on a fire the device delivered.

catchUp.description: `catchUp` marks a fire the device delivered late: no process held the session when the timer came due (its worker was down), so it fires once now, however many times it was missed.

AgentSessionGoalStatus.description: Codex reports active, paused, blocked, usageLimited, budgetLimited or complete; a Claude /goal is active until its condition is met or it is cleared.

AgentSessionGoal.description: AgentSessionGoal is the goal the session's agent works toward on its own, as its runtime reports it: Codex's thread goal (thread/goal/*) or Claude Code's /goal (its active_goal message).

objective.description: The objective (Codex) or the condition Claude checks before it stops.

tokensUsed.description: Tokens Codex spent on the goal so far.

timeUsedSeconds.description: Time Codex spent on the goal so far.

iterations.description: How often Claude's check found the condition not yet met.

lastReason.description: Why Claude's last check found the condition not yet met.

AgentSessionGoalSnapshot.description: The session's goal at the time of the event (latest wins); without `goal` the goal was cleared or met.

WorkerFailure.description: WorkerFailure is a versioned diagnosis; the server preserves it without guessing causes.

inputId.description: Bind diagnostics to a dispatch, never to an earlier turn of the chat.

taskOutputFile.description: `taskOutputFile` is a Claude background task's own output log. Workers before it sent that path, and every changed workspace file, as outputFile; that key is no longer read, so those guesses stay hidden.

sessionFile.description: A file the session's tools wrote or its answer named, once per turn.

toolFrame.description: `toolFrame` is a screenshot a tool call produced, kept as a session file on the device (DEV-075).

fileReferences.description: Paths the turn's answer names that the device verified (turn end).

timerSnapshot.description: Snapshots replace earlier ones, so an empty one is kept: it says the last timer or task is gone.

backgroundTaskSnapshot.description: The session's background work at the time of the event (latest wins): running tasks and the most recent finished ones.

timerFire.description: Present on events marking an automatic timer-triggered background turn.

goalSnapshot.description: The session's goal changed (set, progressed, paused, cleared or met).

turnUsage.description: Present on the event that ends a turn the provider reported usage for.

subagentUsage.description: `subagentUsage` is what a Claude subagent has used so far, on its progress and completion events.

requestUsage.description: `requestUsage` is a model request's tokens, reported when Claude's stream ends or from Codex's native token-usage update; the event itself is not shown.

contextUsage.description: `contextUsage` is how full the session's context is after a main-agent model request or a compaction; the newest counts.

codexTransport.description: `codexTransport` is what a Codex session showed about its compatible endpoint's Responses WebSocket; the server keeps it for the profile.

sentBySessionId.description: `sentBySessionId`, on a message's event (its input, or a message steered into a running turn), is the session that sent it; empty for what the person typed. Viewers resolve its title themselves, as far as they may read that session.

SessionExecutionBudget.description: SessionInput is one message delivered to a session: the unit of dispatch. It is not a session of its own; identity, permissions and lineage belong to the session it was sent to.

at.description: When the server received the input; its transcript events carry it.

timerFire.description: `timerFire` is set when the input is a timer's prompt: its device resumed the session because the timer was due while no agent process ran it. Its transcript event shows the timer firing.

sentBySessionId.description: `sentBySessionId` is the session that sent the input (create_session's first message, send_message); its transcript event names it.

AgentSession.description: AgentSession is one native agent session (a Claude Code or Codex session) for its whole life. Conversation turns stay inside the native agent; the session carries its latest input and the status of handling it.

createdByUserId.description: `createdByUserId` is the account that started it; agent-created sessions inherit their parent's. Set by the server, never by clients.

nativeSessionId.description: `nativeSessionId` is the native session it resumes on the runtime it runs on (its provider on its device); empty starts one there. The store owns every native session a session ran (sqlitestore native_sessions.go); this is that record's projection.

forkNativeSessionId.description: `forkNativeSessionId`, set while a fork has not answered yet, is the native session NativeSessionID starts as a copy of.

workerGroupId.description: The worker group this session's provider and model were picked from, once at creation. The session keeps that member.

dispatchId.description: Identifies this dispatch of the current input. It equals the input id until an automatic retry gives the same logical input a fresh native execution identity.

source.description: "digest": a Personal Agent digest summary session (read-only).

role.description: `role` is the job the session does for Foundry; empty for a chat. AgentSessionRoleIssueExecution implements an Issue's confirmed contract in its candidate workspace; AgentSessionRoleIssueClarification talks the Issue through with the person, read-only.

workspaceAccess.description: `workspaceAccess` read: the session's workspace is read-only for its agent and every command it runs, kept so by the worker's sandbox (a message channel's session, DEV-203); its temporary files go to a scratch directory outside the workspace. Absent: the session writes its workspace as usual.

parentSessionId.description: `parentSessionId` records orchestration lineage: the agent session that created this one. Empty for human/browser chats. It is a record for display and limits, never a source of permission.

waitingChildCount.description: `waitingChildCount` is how many direct sub-sessions this session is waiting on: active turns whose current input it started, or ended children that are themselves waiting on such descendants up to four levels deep. Absent or 0 when none.

questionsTo.description: `questionsTo`, set by the server on dispatch, is who answers the session's questions and permission prompts: "person", who holds this chat (a prompt waits in the turn for a while); "parent", the session that created it, reached through its inbox (a prompt ends the turn and its answer is the next message; with no live parent it waits in this chat). Absent: nobody, and prompts are denied at once.

issueId.description: `issueId` runs the session inside an existing Issue candidate worktree instead of the workspace root, enabling safe parallel writes.

groupNameTarget.description: `groupNameTarget` marks a source=naming utility session whose response should rename the auto-created orchestration group with this id.

createdGroupId.description: `createdGroupId` is populated on a session that caused a new orchestration group to be created, so the HTTP layer can trigger async naming.

blockedReason.description: Present for the active status "blocked" (rate limit / permission wait).

input.description: `input` is the latest message sent to the session; Status describes it.

skillRefs.description: Server-resolved workspace skill selection for this session. The runtime is forced to expose only these; an empty present list means none.

response.description: `response` is the answer to the latest input.

activityAt.description: `activityAt` is its last conversation activity: the latest input, or the answer that completed it. Chat lists order by it.

scheduled.description: `scheduled` is set while the agent holds timers that will wake the session; the store keeps it from the session's timer snapshots.

SkillBundleTool.description: SkillBundleTool is a program a bundle needs, installable from the repository's GitHub release of the bundle's version.

assets.description: `assets` are the release downloads per platform.

checksumsUrl.description: `checksumsUrl` is the release's checksum list, when it publishes one.

source.description: `source` is where it installs from: "" (a GitHub release download), "npm" (the npm package Package at Version), "uv" (the Python package Package at Version, through uv) or "repository" (files at Path in the bundle repository at commit Version).

registry.description: `registry` is where an npm tool installs from: "" the public registry, an https URL that registry, or "device" each device's own npm settings (its npmrc and scoped registries).

repository.description: For a repository tool, the upstream git repository. Version is the commit the bundle recorded, so the tool and Skills are always from one upstream revision.

path.description: The folder in the repository holding the tool's files.

bins.description: Commands to expose, mapped to files relative to Path. The bundle tool Name must be one of them.

setup.description: `setup` is a step the tool needs after installing (e.g. downloading its browser), run only when the person asks.

signIn.description: `signIn` is the command a person runs once in a terminal on each device after installing (e.g. "auth login"); Foundry only shows it.

SkillToolSetup.description: SkillToolSetup runs one of the installed package's commands with fixed arguments.

command.description: `command` is a command the package installs; empty is the tool itself.

description.description: `description` says what it does, e.g. "Downloads Chrome for Testing".

SkillToolAsset.description: SkillToolAsset is one platform's download of a tool.

SkillDependencyStrength.description: One local skill observed by a device scan.

promotedSkillId.description: Set once this exact entry has been promoted to the server catalog.

dependencies.description: Other installed skills this one references, inferred statically.

sourceDigest.description: SHA-256 of the complete source tree used to build this graph node.

PromotedSkill.description: PromotedSkill is a server catalog entry. Content lives in revisions.

usedByWorkspaces.description: `usedByWorkspaces`: the store lists workspace ids; the API answers with the names of the ones the caller can see.

requires.description: `requires` names the programs the latest revision runs.

SessionSkillRef.description: SessionSkillRef is a resolved (skill, revision) pair attached to a dispatched session. Checksum/ByteSize let the worker verify its cache.

sourceDigest.description: `sourceDigest` authenticates the expanded files independently of ZIP encoding.

bundle.description: `bundle` names the bundle the skill came with, so a session can be told about a large bundle as one entry instead of skill by skill.

SessionSkillBundle.description: SessionSkillBundle is the bundle a session skill came with.

SkillFileInfo.description: SkillFileInfo is cached metadata; file contents are loaded on demand.

UsageStatsCostSource.description: One cost_source's share of a usage group.

UsageStatsPoint.description: One time bucket and selected dimension combination.

bucket.description: An RFC 3339 hour boundary or a YYYY-MM-DD day.

provider.description: The profile/provider label recorded with the usage.

averageTokensPerSecond.description: Output tokens divided by measured generation time.

medianTokensPerSecond.description: Median output tokens per second across measured requests.

ttftP50Ms.description: Median first-token latency across measured requests.

WorkspaceKind.description: Every workspace is a project except each person's Personal Agent Workspace.

accessRole.description: `accessRole` is the caller's role in the workspace, set per request.

unavailableOnDevice.description: `unavailableOnDevice` is set while its device, connected, does not serve the folder. Its sessions and history stay; adding the folder on the device again clears it.

kind.description: `kind` is WorkspaceKindProject (sent as absent) or WorkspaceKindPersonalAgent.

archivedAt.description: `archivedAt` is set while the workspace is archived: hidden in an "Archived" group, starting no sessions, everything kept.

migration.description: `migration` is the workspace's move to another device (DEV-146) still under way, or the latest completed one whose old copy on the source device was not deleted yet.

WorkspaceMigrationState.description: preflight, copying, verifying, activating, retiring, then complete; canceled and failed end it too. While copying, verifying or activating the workspace is frozen: no new sessions or messages run there.

WorkspaceMigrationSummary.description: WorkspaceMigrationSummary is what the workspace list shows of a move: the one under way, else the latest complete one whose old copy was not deleted, else the latest move when it failed. A canceled move is never shown.

WorkspaceMigrationFolderWarning.description: Something in the folder that does not travel as it is (the source scan's warnings).

WorkspaceMigrationBlocker.description: Work in the workspace that must end before it can move.

WorkspaceMigrationNotCarried.description: A setting of the workspace tied to the source device; it is not moved and has to be set up again on the target device.

WorkspaceMigrationSourcePurge.description: Whether the old copy on the source device was deleted. A delete that kept files changed after the move leaves state none and records lastAttemptAt and keptCount.

lastAttemptAt.description: When a delete last ran that kept changed files.

keptCount.description: How many changed paths that delete kept.

WorkspaceMigration.description: WorkspaceMigration moves a workspace, same id and history, to a folder on another device (docs/devlog/DEV-146-workspace-migration.md).

step.description: The current sub-step, a short machine word: queued, checking, scanning, checking_target, streaming, retrying, copying_changes, verifying_target, rescanning, activating_target, retiring_source, aborting, done.

files.description: Files received on the target so far.

reason.description: Why it failed or what it waits for, in English; "" when nothing to say.

reasonCode.description: Machine code of reason, for the Web to localize: device_offline, worker_outdated, target_path_taken, target_path_unavailable, not_enough_space, workspace_busy, device_refused, transfer_retrying, transfer_failed, verify_mismatch, canceled_by_person. The migration routes answer errors as {code, error}; their codes: invalid_request, same_device, folder_missing, migration_active, device_offline, target_path_taken (start); no_migration (current); not_cancelable (cancel); not_complete, already_purged, device_offline, device_refused, worker_outdated (purge-source).

WorkspaceMigrationPurgePreview.description: What deleting the old copy removes (confirm false: nothing removed yet) and which paths it keeps because they changed after the move.

WorkspaceUnavailability.description: WorkspaceUnavailability says why a workspace cannot run on its device.

WorkspaceNativeSessionsMoved.description: WorkspaceNativeSessionsMoved is what relinking did to make the workspace's native sessions resumable in its new folder.

copied.description: Native sessions now resumable in the new folder (copied there).

alreadyThere.description: Already resumable there (nothing to do, e.g. Codex, keyed by id).

notFound.description: Not found on the device: their chats continue in a new native session that is given the Foundry conversation.

WorkspaceRelinkSuggestion.description: WorkspaceRelinkSuggestion is a folder that looks like a missing workspace's, moved: "same_workspace" or "same_git_remote".

reason.description: "same_workspace": the folder holds this workspace's own Foundry identity (.foundry/workspace.json), so it is the folder, moved or renamed. "same_git_remote": its Git repository has the same origin remote.

revision.description: Device content identity for bounded instruction files.
